# 🍎 macOS Systems & Darwin Engineering Track

Welcome to the **macOS Systems & Darwin Engineering Track** materialized by **Trak**.

This workspace is an in-depth curriculum covering Darwin kernel architecture (XNU), APFS filesystem mechanics, launchd service management, Homebrew packaging, Apple Silicon universal binaries, and macOS security (SIP, Gatekeeper, TCC).

## 📚 Syllabus & Module Map

| Module | Title | Key Topics & Internals |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-darwin-architecture` | Darwin & XNU Kernel | XNU architecture (Mach microkernel + BSD), `sw_vers`, System Integrity Protection (SIP) |
| `01-homebrew-and-package-management` | Homebrew & Brew Services | `/opt/homebrew` (ARM64) vs `/usr/local` (Intel), `brew cask`, `brew services` |
| `02-zsh-and-macos-shell-environment` | Zsh & Terminal Config | `.zshrc`, `.zprofile`, environment variables, macOS default shell |
| `03-file-system-apfs-and-extended-attributes` | APFS & Extended Attributes | Copy-on-write clones, snapshots, extended attributes (`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine`) |
| `04-launchd-services-and-daemons` | `launchd` & Plist Daemons | LaunchDaemons vs LaunchAgents, plist XML format, `launchctl bootstrap/bootout` |
| `05-process-management-and-activity-monitor` | Processes & Thermal States | `ps`, `top`, thermal state monitoring (`pmset -g therm`), memory pressure |
| `06-macos-system-preferences-and-defaults` | `defaults` & Plist Editing | `defaults write com.apple.finder`, `plutil -p`, system preference domains |
| `07-security-gatekeeper-sip-and-tcc` | Gatekeeper, SIP & TCC | Gatekeeper quarantine, `csrutil status`, TCC privacy permissions DB |
| `08-networking-scutil-and-networksetup` | macOS Networking & DNS | `networksetup`, `scutil --dns`, `dscacheutil -flushcache`, dynamic DNS |
| `09-applescript-and-jxa` | Automation & `osascript` | AppleScript (`osascript -e`), JavaScript for Automation (JXA), UI automation |
| `10-diskutil-and-storage-management` | `diskutil` & Disk Images | `diskutil apfs`, APFS containers, `hdiutil attach/detach` DMG images |
| `11-developer-toolchain-xcode-and-metal` | Xcode CLI & Toolchain | `xcode-select --install`, `xcrun`, LLVM clang on macOS, Metal shaders |
| `12-universal-binaries-and-rosetta` | Universal 2 & Rosetta 2 | Mach-O fat binaries (`lipo -info`), Rosetta 2 translation (`arch -x86_64`) |
| `13-keychain-and-credential-security` | Keychain Access (`security`) | Secure credential storage, `security find-generic-password`, certificates |
| `14-power-management-and-pmset` | Power Management & `pmset` | Sleep assertions, battery health, `caffeinate` CLI utility |
| `15-logging-unified-logging-system` | Unified Logging System | `log stream --predicate`, `log show`, subsystems & categories |
| `16-automator-and-shortcuts-cli` | Shortcuts CLI & Automator | `shortcuts run`, Quick Actions, headless workflow automation |
| `17-testing-and-diagnostics` | Diagnostics & Sysdiagnose | `sysdiagnose`, kernel crash logs, diagnostic reports in `/Library/Logs` |
| `18-interview-questions-and-drills` | Interview Mastery Drills | Top 10 macOS Systems & Enterprise MDM gotchas + Production Diagnostic Drill |

---

## 🛠️ How to Practice
Each module contains:
- `README.md` — Deep theoretical explanation and architecture notes.
- `example.sh` — Fully runnable concept demonstration.
- `exercise/starter.sh` — Hands-on problem with `TODO` markers.
- `exercise/solution.sh` — Complete reference solution.

# 00 — Setup And Darwin Architecture

## 🎯 What is it?
Setup And Darwin Architecture is a core foundational concept in macOS Systems & Darwin Engineering that governs how resources, execution flow, and system state are managed.

## 💡 Why does it exist & Why use it?
Without mastering Setup And Darwin Architecture, systems suffer from subtle bugs, suboptimal performance, security vulnerabilities, or unpredictable runtime behavior. Understanding this concept allows you to design reliable, production-grade solutions.

## ⚙️ How does it work under the hood?
Under the hood, Setup And Darwin Architecture executes through structured lifecycle phases: initialization, state validation, execution against target constraints, and deterministic result propagation to calling layers.

## 🔍 Concept & Core Logic
**Core Logic & Mental Model**
- Establishes explicit boundaries between declarative intent and runtime execution.
- Preserves deterministic behavior and state isolation across distributed or concurrent environments.

**Technical Internals & Architectural Notes:**
— Darwin & XNU Kernel Architecture

## 🎯 What is XNU?
XNU ("X is Not Unix") is the hybrid operating system kernel powering macOS, iOS, and watchOS:
- **Mach Microkernel**: Handles IPC, thread scheduling, virtual memory (`vm_map`), and CPU core dispatching.
- **BSD Subsystem**: Provides POSIX APIs, process models, networking stack (BSD sockets), and filesystem interfaces.

## ⏱️ When to use & When NOT to use
**When to Use:** Standard production workflows, automated pipelines, and scalable application architectures requiring high reliability.
**When NOT to Use:** Trivial throwaway scripts where the operational overhead outweighs the benefits.

children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "=== 00: macOS Darwin Architecture ==="
if command -v sw_vers &>/dev/null; then
  sw_vers
  echo "Darwin Kernel: $(uname -v)"
else
  echo "Simulated macOS Environment (sw_vers command not in PATH)"
fi

children.name: starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
ARCH=$(uname -m)
if [ "$ARCH" = "arm64" ]; then
  echo "✔ Apple Silicon Architecture (arm64)"
elif [ "$ARCH" = "x86_64" ]; then
  echo "✔ Intel Architecture (x86_64)"
else
  echo "Unknown architecture: $ARCH"
fi

echo "=== 03: Extended Attributes ==="
touch /tmp/quarantine_demo.txt

solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/dev.trak.agent.plist
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>dev.trak.agent</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>/usr/local/bin/trak</string>
        <string>daemon</string>
    </array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
</plist>
EOF
echo "✔ Generated LaunchAgent plist file."
rm -f /tmp/dev.trak.agent.plist
